summary: The root بَرَزَ (baraza) primarily means to go or come out, to issue forth, or to appear after being hidden.
lane: 1 بَرَزَ برز رز , (S, A, Msb, K,) aor. بَرُزَ , (S, TA,) inf. n. بُرُوزٌ , (S, Msb, TA,) He (a man, S) went, or came, or passed, out, or forth; he issued. (S, A.) He (a man, TA) went, or came, or passed, out, or forth, into the field, plain, or open tract or country: (K:) or did so to satisfy a want of nature: (TS, TA:) as also, in the former sense, (K,) or in the latter, (S,) ; (S, K, TA;) and بَرِزَ ; (Sgh, TA;) and so, in the former sense, inf. n. تَبْرِيزٌ ; (Har p. 510;) [and in the latter sense, accord. to an explanation of its part. n. مُبَارِزٌ in Har p. 566:] or signifies he voided his excrement, or ordure. (Mgh, Msb.) You say, بَرَزَإِلَى القِرْنِ فِى الحَرْبِ He went, or came, out, or forth, into the field to his adversary in battle or war. (TA.) -b2- He, or it, (a man, TA, or thing, Msb, or anything, Fr,) appeared, or became apparent, (Fr, Sgh, Msb, K,) after concealment, (Fr, K,) or after obscurity; (Sgh;) as also بَرِزَ (Sgh, K.) -b3- [ It was, or became, prominent, or projecting: often used in this sense.] -A2- بَرُزَ , (Msb, K,) inf. n. بَرَازَةٌ , (Msb,) He (a man) was, or became, such as is termed بَرْزٌ q. v.: (Msb, K:) and in like manner, بَرُزَتْ , inf. n. as above, she (a woman) was, or became, such as is termed بَرْزَةٌ (A.)
